correctness.rationale: Shortest paths give powered distance a within a part, 1 across an ordinary pair, and 1+h at the distinguished pair. At fixed part sum S and distinguished entries x,y, subtracting each part's remaining-coordinate mean leaves strictly negative contrast squares; the reduced negative form is the displayed three-variable matrix. Its last block is positive definite since h≤a and mn−(m−1)(n−1)>0. The scalar Schur complement and endpoints check: F(0)=1/m+1/n and F(1)=−2(m+n−5)/(m+n−1). Hence there is a zero in the claimed interval, with precisely one kernel direction. Li–Weston Theorem 5.4 then gives strictness below, excludes negative type above and proves uniqueness; the centered Gram rank gives the stated dimensions. In the balanced block the determinant reduces to T_r=[r−1−(r−2)a][ra+(r−1)h]−a²; T_r(q_r)=3^q_r−1. The equality vector at S=1 has x=−y=a/[ra+(r−1)h], with nonzero coefficients on all undistinguished vertices. Extending by zeros to the next isometric graph gives strict threshold decrease. On [q_r,2/(r log 2)], T_r' = −(log 2)r²+O(r), while T_r(2/(r log 2))=−r+O(1). The mean-value theorem with T_r(q_r)=(log 3/log 2)/r+O(r^-2) yields the claimed coefficient and remainder. Independent bounded bisection agreed between the scalar equations at r=3,4,5,8,16,32,64,128 to 10^-10 and gave p(2,3)=1; it is only corroboration. RESULT.md lines 23–79 constitute the universal proof; frozen verify.py was inspected, not executed.
